slides.text: Formation of Chhattisgarh in chronological order In the 1941 census, the Chhattisgarh region was in Central Provinces and Berar also called C.P. & Berar. In 1854, Chhattisgarh became three divisions, Raipur, Ratanpur, and Dhamtari. Tehsils were reconstituted and 5 Tehsils were established - Raipur, Dhamtari, Ratanpur, Dhamdha, Jawagarh.

slides.text: In the 1951 census, the Chhattisgarh region was with CP and Berar. When the states were formed on a linguistic basis in the year 1956, the then MLA Thakur Ramakrishna Singh demanded the formation of a separate state with the Chhattisgarhi dialect as the basis. In 1920 , Sundarlal Sharma was envisaged in Chhattisgarh state.

slides.text: In 1993, Chhattisgarh was mentioned in Congress ' s election manifesto. In the Madhya Pradesh Assembly Election on March 18, 1994, a separate government resolution related to Chhattisgarh formally and unanimously passed. After the Lok Sabha elections on March 25, 1998, the mention of the formation of a separate Chhattisgarh state in the President ' s address to the joint session of the House.

slides.text: Resolution on the constitution of a separate state of Chhattisgarh in Madhya Pradesh Legislative Assembly on May 1, 1998 Mentioned in the election manifesto of Congress and Bharatiya Janata Party in assembly elections of 1998 The then Prime Minister Late Atal Bihari Bajpai announced in a general meeting that, if Bharatiya Janata Party wins all the 11 Lok Sabha constituencies, then state formation. A bill for the formation of 3 new states in the Lok Sabha on 25 July 2000. On July 25, 2000, the then Home Minister LK Advani presented the Chhattisgarh Amendment Bill 2000 in the Lok Sabha.
